entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Valken Kruger tapped the gavel. The..."
entries.dialogueText:
Valken Kruger tapped the gavel. The sound echoed in the empty courtroom.

He rose from his seat.

Knowing what was coming next, you felt that you...

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...did your best for Sordland. No m..."
entries.dialogueText: ...did your best for Sordland. No matter what.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Iosef Lancea tapped the gavel. The..."
entries.dialogueText:
Iosef Lancea tapped the gavel. The sound echoed in the empty courtroom.

He rose from his seat.

Knowing what was coming next, you felt that you...

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The next words you heard were "I he..."
entries.dialogueText:
The next words you heard were "I hereby decide that you are guilty."

You thought about how you would go down in history as...

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...worried about the future of your..."
entries.dialogueText: ...worried about the future of your family.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...declared that you would take rev..."
entries.dialogueText: ...declared that you would take revenge.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...were angry at everyone who betra..."
entries.dialogueText: ...were angry at everyone who betrayed you.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...blamed only yourself."
entries.dialogueText: ...blamed only yourself.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...the victim of yet another one of..."
entries.dialogueText: ...the victim of yet another one of Sordland's coups.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The gunshots were the last thing yo..."
entries.dialogueText: The gunshots were the last thing you ever heard.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "But he wasn't done speaking. "Fo..."
entries.dialogueText:
But he wasn't done speaking.

"For the magnitude of the crimes you have committed against Sordland, I am sentencing you to life in prison."

Soldiers grabbed your arms and started walking you towards the door. 

As you were walking you...

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "Your whole world fell apart."
entries.dialogueText: Your whole world fell apart.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...accepted your fate."
entries.dialogueText: ...accepted your fate.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...congratulated him."
entries.dialogueText: ...congratulated him.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Your cell was cold and lonely. The..."
entries.dialogueText:
Your cell was cold and lonely. The only decorations you put on the damp, dark walls were photos of Franc and Deana.

For a while, reading was the only thing you could do. After finishing the precious books sent by Monica, you kept yourself busy by writing your own memoir.

You were happy that at least your family was allowed to visit once a month.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...cried like a child."
entries.dialogueText: ...cried like a child.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...defiantly stood proud and strong..."
entries.dialogueText: ...defiantly stood proud and strong.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...felt relaxed. It was finally ove..."
entries.dialogueText: ...felt relaxed. It was finally over.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Your cell was cold and lonely. A we..."
entries.dialogueText:
Your cell was cold and lonely. A week remained until your execution.

To keep busy, you read books and occasionally scribbled down notes about your life that you hoped someone would compile into a memoir. It was better than just staring at the wall and waiting for your certain death.

Monica visited you only once, along with the kids.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "And so Anton Rayne was no more."
entries.dialogueText: And so Anton Rayne was no more.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He covered your eyes and stepped ba..."
entries.dialogueText:
He covered your eyes and stepped back. 

After a moment, you heard the sounds of the guns being cocked.

You...

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Go to hell.""
entries.dialogueText: "Go to hell."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""A Morgna wes core! Vectern sis da!""
entries.dialogueText: "A Morgna wes core! Vectern sis da!"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I regret nothing.""
entries.dialogueText: "I regret nothing."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Your cell was cold and lonely. You..."
entries.dialogueText:
Your cell was cold and lonely. You had a week until your execution.

To keep busy, you read books and occasionally scribbled down notes about your life that you hoped someone would compile into a memoir. It was better than just staring at the wall and waiting for your certain death.

You were happy that at least your family was allowed to visit you every day.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Franc visited you for the first tim..."
entries.dialogueText:
Franc visited you for the first time in years, bringing along his wife and son. They reminded you of your own family, in better times.

You held your grandson for the first time. He squirmed and started crying in your arms.

Franc told you that he had joined the ranks of the Communist Party of Sordland. You...

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He asked you if you had any last wo..."
entries.dialogueText: He asked you if you had any last words.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...told him not to get too deep int..."
entries.dialogueText: ...told him not to get too deep into politics.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "Accept your death."
entries.dialogueText: Accept your death.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "Beg Iosef to free you."
entries.dialogueText: Beg Iosef to free you.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Franc visited you for the first tim..."
entries.dialogueText:
Franc visited you for the first time in years, bringing along his wife and son. They reminded you of your own family, in better times.

You held your grandson for the first time. He squirmed and started crying in your arms.

Franc told you that he was now a senior army official on a track to the higher ranks. You...

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The squad of soldiers turned the co..."
entries.dialogueText:
The squad of soldiers turned the corner and lined up across from you. At the head of the line was their commander, Iosef.

He checked his watch and declared that the time had come. 

He pulled out a cloth to cover your eyes.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...said you were worried for his fu..."
entries.dialogueText: ...said you were worried for his future.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "But he wasn't finished speaking...."
entries.dialogueText:
But he wasn't finished speaking.

"For the magnitude of the crimes you have committed against Sordland, I am sentencing you to execution by firing squad."

Soldiers grabbed your arms and started walking you towards the door. 

As you were walking you...

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "You heard the footsteps of soldiers..."
entries.dialogueText: You heard the footsteps of soldiers approaching.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...worried about the future of your..."
entries.dialogueText: ...worried about the future of your family.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...declared that you would take rev..."
entries.dialogueText: ...declared that you would take revenge.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...accepted your fate."
entries.dialogueText: ...accepted your fate.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You were dragged outside after you..."
entries.dialogueText:
You were dragged outside after you finished your final meal. Soldiers brought you to a corner just outside the prison block and tied your hands behind your back.

You took a look at the wall behind you. It was covered in dried blood.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Franc visited you for the first tim..."
entries.dialogueText:
Franc visited you for the first time in years, bringing along his wife and son. They reminded you of your own family, in better times.

You held your grandson for the first time. He squirmed and started crying in your arms.

Franc told you that he had joined the ranks of the People's Freedom and Justice Party. You...

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Your cell was cold and lonely. The..."
entries.dialogueText:
Your cell was cold and lonely. The only decorations you put on the damp, dark walls were photos of Franc and Deana.

For a while, reading books was the only thing you could do. Eventually, you started scribbling notes about your life that you hoped you could turn into a memoir.

Monica and the children visited only once, to have you sign the divorce papers.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...a bottle of whiskey."
entries.dialogueText: ...a bottle of whiskey.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "Time flies in jail."
entries.dialogueText: Time flies in jail.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...a hearty and healthy breakfast."
entries.dialogueText: ...a hearty and healthy breakfast.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...the largest, bloodiest steak he..."
entries.dialogueText: ...the largest, bloodiest steak he could find.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "The week was over."
entries.dialogueText: The week was over.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The day of your execution had arriv..."
entries.dialogueText:
The day of your execution had arrived.

The cell door opened and the warden entered. He asked you what would be your final meal.

You asked him for...

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The squad of soldiers turned the co..."
entries.dialogueText:
The squad of soldiers turned the corner and lined up across from you. At the head of the line was their commander, Valken.

He checked his watch and declared that the time had come. 

He pulled out a cloth to cover your eyes.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "Beg Valken to free you."
entries.dialogueText: Beg Valken to free you.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You learned in prison that after 2..."
entries.dialogueText:
You learned in prison that after 2 years, the military junta finally gave the power back to people.

The political parties and the Grand National Assembly were re-established.

You...

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...did not care much."
entries.dialogueText: ...did not care much.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...thought that this could be your..."
entries.dialogueText: ...thought that this could be your way out.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...hoped that someone would hang Io..."
entries.dialogueText: ...hoped that someone would hang Iosef for his crimes.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...hoped that someone would hang Va..."
entries.dialogueText: ...hoped that someone would hang Valken for his crimes.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "After 7 years in jail, Sordland's n..."
entries.dialogueText:
After 7 years in jail, Sordland's new president finally granted amnesty to political prisoners from the military rule days.

You looked at yourself in the mirror as you were packing up your belongings to leave.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "You had grown old."
entries.dialogueText: You had grown old.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Getting used to being a free man to..."
entries.dialogueText:
Getting used to being a free man took years.

You finally felt confident enough to plan out what to do with the rest of your life.

You chose to...

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You took your first step outside. F..."
entries.dialogueText:
You took your first step outside. Freedom felt good.

No one was waiting for you.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You took your first step outside. F..."
entries.dialogueText:
You took your first step outside. Freedom felt good.

Franc and his family were waiting for you. 

Everything had changed so much that you felt out of place.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You took your first step outside. F..."
entries.dialogueText:
You took your first step outside. Freedom felt good.

Monica, Deana and Franc were waiting for you.

Unfortunately, the years hadn't been kind to Monica.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You took your first step outside. F..."
entries.dialogueText:
You took your first step outside. Freedom felt good.

Monica and Deana were waiting for you.

Unfortunately, the years hadn't been kind to Monica.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "The years haven't been kind to you."
entries.dialogueText: The years haven't been kind to you.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "But they hadn't been kind to you ei..."
entries.dialogueText: But they hadn't been kind to you either.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...have another shot at politics."
entries.dialogueText: ...have another shot at politics.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...retire to the countryside."
entries.dialogueText: ...retire to the countryside.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...find an earnest job."
entries.dialogueText: ...find an earnest job.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You tried to get back into politics..."
entries.dialogueText:
You tried to get back into politics, but Sordland had changed too much.

The political spheres formed after the coup did not accept you.

You had to work menial, though at least honest, jobs to get by.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Life was good. You took up vario..."
entries.dialogueText:
Life was good.

You took up various hobbies like gardening and woodworking. Out of boredom, you became a carpenter.

Your new past times earned you just enough money to get by.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "At least you were free."
entries.dialogueText: At least you were free.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Life was good. You took up woodw..."
entries.dialogueText:
Life was good.

You took up woodworking and became a carpenter.

It was a menial job, but at least it was honest.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "You had all the time in the world."
entries.dialogueText: You had all the time in the world.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "You had to get by somehow."
entries.dialogueText: You had to get by somehow.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A week after your 66th birthday, a..."
entries.dialogueText:
A week after your 66th birthday, a woman knocked on your door.

She was a young upstart journalist fascinated by your life story. No matter what you did, she kept coming back. Finally, you gave in. She said she was working on a book about you. 

You...

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...just wanted to finally have peac..."
entries.dialogueText: ...just wanted to finally have peace of mind.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "...helped her as best as you could."
entries.dialogueText: ...helped her as best as you could.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "After many hours of interviews, she..."
entries.dialogueText:
After many hours of interviews, she said that she had enough information and disappeared from your life.

You looked up the name she had given you, but you couldn't find it anywhere. You suspected she'd used an alias.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "You wondered why."
entries.dialogueText: You wondered why.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "You heard a knock on your door. It..."
entries.dialogueText:
You heard a knock on your door. It was the delivery man with a large, heavy package.

The package was filled with copies of books. There was a small note on top of it.

"Thank you. --Carol Circas"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "You picked up the book."
entries.dialogueText: You picked up the book.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "It was titled Suzerain: The Story o..."
entries.dialogueText: It was titled Suzerain: The Story of Anton Rayne.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "You faintly smiled."
entries.dialogueText: You faintly smiled.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The warden paid you a visit to deli..."
entries.dialogueText:
The warden paid you a visit to deliver a letter from the Sordish Armed Forces. You opened the envelope.

Franc Rayne was killed in action in a battle against the BFF near Erzaren.
